title: "If Something Happens" Family Information Binder (PDF) — $19
description: A fillable binder that tells your family where documents are, who to call and which accounts exist, without storing passwords. Not a will. $19.
outcome: Leave the people you trust a clear map of your documents, contacts, accounts and wishes, so they are not searching through drawers in a crisis.
benefits: 10-page fillable PDF: contacts, legal documents, money, home, digital life, dependents, wishes
Designed for safety: no fields for passwords, PINs or full account numbers
Digital accounts page built around legacy contacts and password-manager emergency access
Companion spreadsheet for long lists of accounts, policies and documents
Annual review log so it stays current

steps: Open the PDF in Adobe Acrobat Reader or your browser, or print it.
Start with emergency contacts and where your legal documents are.
List accounts and policies by institution and last 4 digits only.
Tell one trusted person where the binder is kept.
Review it once a year with the log on the last page.
forWho: Parents, caregivers and anyone who manages household paperwork
Adults helping aging parents get organized
Anyone who has (or is about to make) a will and wants their family to find things
notFor: Anyone looking for a will, trust or power of attorney: this binder is not a legal document
People who want to store passwords: use a password manager with emergency access instead
compat: PDF fillable in Adobe Acrobat Reader and most browser PDF viewers (save a copy after filling); printable on US Letter. Spreadsheet works in Excel, Google Sheets and LibreOffice.
limits: It does not make or replace a will, trust, power of attorney or advance directive.
It does not give anyone legal authority to act for you.
It deliberately does not store passwords or full account numbers.

faq.a: No. It records where your documents are and what your wishes are, but it has no legal effect. Wills, powers of attorney and advance directives must meet your state's legal formalities.

faq.q: Why are there no password fields?
faq.a: A binder with passwords and full account numbers is a security risk if it is lost or seen by the wrong person. The binder points to safer tools such as legacy contacts and password-manager emergency access.
